curriculum.subject: Mathematical Activities
curriculum.outcomeText: appreciate the beauty of patterns in different fabrics.

mission.title: appreciate the beauty of patterns in different fabrics.

interactions.prompt: Look at the kitenge cloth. Which shape repeats?
interactions.feedback: Yes! Triangles repeat to make this cloth pattern beautiful.
interactions.retryHint: Look for the shape that comes again and again.

interactions.prompt: Watch the pattern: circle, rectangle, circle, rectangle. What comes next?
interactions.feedback: Great looking! The circle starts the pattern again.
interactions.retryHint: Say the repeating part: circle, rectangle.

interactions.prompt: Make a fabric border. Tap the shapes in this order: triangle, triangle, circle.
interactions.tapAlternative: Tap the shapes in the order shown; dragging is not needed.
interactions.feedback: Lovely! Your triangle, triangle, circle border has a repeating part.
interactions.retryHint: Start with two triangles. Then add one circle.

interactions.prompt: A Maasai shuka pattern goes oval, oval, rectangle, oval, oval, rectangle. What comes next?
interactions.feedback: Correct! The pattern begins again with an oval.
interactions.retryHint: Find the small group that repeats: oval, oval, rectangle.

interactions.prompt: Finish this cloth strip. Tap the next two shapes after circle, triangle, rectangle, circle.
interactions.tapAlternative: Tap triangle, then rectangle to finish the strip.
interactions.feedback: Beautiful work! You continued the cloth pattern correctly.
interactions.retryHint: Repeat the group: circle, triangle, rectangle.

interactions.prompt: Which fabric strip has a repeating pattern?
interactions.feedback: Excellent! Repeating shapes can make fabric look beautiful.
interactions.retryHint: Choose the strip with the same small shape group repeated.
